answer.why_different: The generated side introduces a different structure: it adds a `callbacks.removed` entry whose value is an array of four path-like strings, rather than omitting the callback. This is likely a malformed representation of callback-related locations, not a valid OpenAPI Callback Object.
answer.spec_3gpp: The supplied 3GPP evidence describes notifications, including `notifyMOIDeletion`, as HTTP POST operations sent to `{notificationTarget}`. It does not support adding a callback named `removed` to this PUT operation, nor does it define the generated array structure.
answer.openapi: The generated value is not valid OpenAPI 3.0. An operation's `callbacks` field must be a map whose values are Callback Objects or Reference Objects, and each callback expression must map to a Path Item Object. The generated value is an array of strings instead.
answer.clearer_why: The official side avoids an invalid callback structure. The generated side is not understandable as a valid callback definition because its value is an array of internal path descriptions rather than a callback object.

##### Runtime Expressions  
Runtime expressions allow defining values based on information that will only be available within the HTTP message in an actual API call.
This mechanism is used by [Link Objects](#link-object) and [Callback Objects](#callback-object).  
The runtime expression is defined by the following [ABNF](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5234) syntax  
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )

evidence.text:
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
